summary.oneLiner: Shree Pushkar delivered steady FY26 growth (21% revenue) but strategically halted dispatches and delayed Unit 5/6 commissioning in Q4 due to tripled raw material costs (Ammonia/Sulphur) outpacing subsidy adjustments. Management prioritizes margin protection over volume, expecting a 'blessing' of inventory gains in Q1FY27 while deferring new capacity contribution until market pricing stabilizes.

one-line thesis: Shree Pushkar delivered steady FY26 growth (21% revenue) but strategically halted dispatches and delayed Unit 5/6 commissioning in Q4 due to tripled raw material costs (Ammonia/Sulphur) outpacing subsidy adjustments. Management prioritizes margin protection over volume, expecting a 'blessing' of inventory gains in Q1FY27 while deferring new capacity contribution until market pricing stabilizes.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs. 976.6 Cr (+21.1% YoY); Q4 Rev: Rs. 218.2 Cr. EBITDA: Rs. 99.5 Cr (10.2% margin); Q4 EBITDA: Rs. 22.1 Cr (10.1%). PAT: Rs. 70.1 Cr (7.1% margin); Q4 PAT: Rs. 12.9 Cr (5.8%). One-offs: Deferred tax charge of Rs. 4-4.5 Cr on land capitalization (Ind AS) and leasehold provisions suppressed PAT; underlying operational PAT closer to 8%. Order Book: N/A (Commodity/Spot sales). Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash Rs. 140.68 Cr deposits); Net Debt/EBITDA -0.05x.
guidance: Revenue Growth: FY27 guidance lowered to Rs. 1,250-1,300 Cr (from Rs. 1,500 Cr) due to lost Kharif season contribution from new units. Margin: Targeting 8-10% EBITDA/PAT mix; conservative 8% PAT visibility. Order Inflow: Deliberately suppressed in March Q4 to capture April-June price hikes. Capex/Commissioning: Unit 5 & 6 (90-95% complete) held back; trial production possible within 1 month but commercially paused until raw material (Ammonia/Sulphur) pricing stabilizes; likely commissioning Q1/Q2 FY27.
order book & pipeline: No formal order book; spot market driven. Management intentionally withheld ~Rs. 24 Cr sales in late March Q4 to realize higher realizations in Q1FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail: Chemical Segment: FY26 Rev Rs. 531.8 Cr (+25.2%); Volume 72,423 MT (+27.9%). Q4 Rev Rs. 126.4 Cr; Volume 13,725 MT (+36% YoY). Realization up despite volume surge (H-Acid Rs. 525->750/kg; Vinyl Sulphone Rs. 240->350/kg). Fertiliser Segment: FY26 Rev Rs. 444.8 Cr (+16.5%); Volume 252,777 MT. Q4 Rev Rs. 91.8 Cr; Volume 50,500 MT. Growth driven by improved realization offsetting volume constraints from RM shortage.
growth verticals / optionality: Unit 5 (Dyes) and Unit 6 (Fertiliser expansion) ready for trial but commercially paused to avoid working capital strain at peak input costs. Meghnagar expansion (Rs. 350 Cr capex) in planning; funding via internal accruals (Rs. 170 Cr available) + potential minor debt (25-30%). Solar capacity expanding to 20.6 MW DC (1.1 MW commissioned in Haryana; 10 MW Nanded in progress).
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin Q4: 38.4%. EBITDA Margin Q4: 10.1%. Cost Pressure: Ammonia Rs. 40->100+/kg; Sulphur Rs. 30->100/kg. Government NBS subsidy increased but capped at 10% hike, insufficient to cover 3x input cost rise. Management expects margin recovery to 8-10% range as finished goods prices re-rate higher in Q1FY27.
capex / expansion: Total Planned: Rs. 512 Cr. Incurred by Mar'26: Rs. 189 Cr. Recent tranche (Rs. 155 Cr): Unit 5 Dyes (Rs. 37 Cr), Solar (Rs. 35 Cr), Unit 6 (Rs. 85 Cr). Funded via Internal Accruals (Rs. 130 Cr) + Term Loan (Rs. 25 Cr HDFC for Solar). Future Meghnagar project (Rs. 350 Cr) to be funded largely by internal accruals.
capital allocation: Debt-free core operations; Net Cash position. Rs. 140.68 Cr in non-lien AAA-rated bonds. Preferential allotment (Rs. 30 Cr) to promoters completed. Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but capital preservation for expansion prioritized. No major debt planned for upcoming capex (<30% leverage max).
risks & watch-items: Sustained raw material inflation (Ammonia/Sulphur) exceeding pass-through ability. Global geopolitical instability affecting energy/feedstock supply. Delay in commissioning Unit 5/6 beyond Q2FY27 leading to further revenue miss. Government subsidy policy changes. Demand suppression in Bangladesh/Global markets due to energy crisis.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic but highly defensive. 'Sit quietly, wait and watch.' Prioritizes long-term survival over short-term volume. Transparent about delaying revenue to protect margins. Views volatility as a 'blessing' for well-capitalized players. Conservative guidance to manage expectations.
non-obvious takeaways: Management deliberately stopped sales in mid-March Q4 (forgoing ~Rs. 24 Cr revenue) to sell inventory in Q1FY27 at significantly higher prices, creating a hidden Q1 earnings boost. Unit 5 & 6 are physically complete but financially uncapitalized to avoid depreciation/working capital drag during peak input costs. The 'lost' Kharif season is a strategic choice, not a failure of execution.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Triple-digit raw material inflation (Ammonia/Sulphur) squeezing margins for non-integrated players; subsidy lag. | Shree Pushkar Chemicals & Fertilisers Ltd | beneficiary | High | Integrated structure and strong balance sheet allow strategic inventory holding and production pausing, turning industry-wide cost crisis into a Q1FY27 margin expansion opportunity while weaker competitors face cash flow stress. |

themes.title: Fertilizer subsidy & nutrient-policy cycle
themes.need: Fertilizer makers are driven by NBS/urea subsidy policy, gas-pooling and nutrient pricing rather than the crop-protection volume/molecule-launch recovery. Q1FY27's supply-side read comes from MBAPL: revenue roughly flat at INR 416cr with EBITDA +16% and PAT +17% purely on cheap March-bought raw material that management said is now EXHAUSTED, with utilisation only ~43-45% because of raw-material availability rather than demand - SSP sales were +28% and NPK +33% YoY against production down 7%/28%. Its Dhule (Maharashtra) integrated complex commissions +3,30,000 MTPA DAP-NPK plus 99,000 MTPA phosphoric acid in Oct-2026 and a second phase in Oct-2027, framed as a >50% turnover jump toward ~INR 3,500cr revenue and 15.6 lakh MT capacity by FY28; Egypt/Jordan rock-phosphate sourcing (non-Hormuz) insulated it relative to import-dependent peers. Subsidy clarity and gas costs still set the near-term margin.
themes.driver: NBS/urea subsidy policy (the Oct-Mar rate revision), gas-pooling and nutrient pricing; MBAPL's Oct-2026 Dhule commissioning and the utilisation ramp toward ~90%; kharif demand pull-through after a delayed monsoon.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Zero-Waste, Integrated Manufacturing Model": "Interlinked manufacturing setup anchored by the Acid Complex, enabling seamless by-product utilization across divisions" and "Integrated operations optimizing resource and raw material utilization while strengthening cost efficiency across the value chain".
- Six-vertical presence stated on the letterhead — "Speciality Textile Dyes, Dyes Intermediates, Acids, Power, Animal Health & Nutrition, Fertilisers" — with FY26 revenue split as "Fertilisers (46% FY26 Revenue)" and "Chemicals (54% FY26 Revenue)".
- "Comprehensive Manufacturing & Distribution Network": 9 facilities across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana, "800+ distributors and 14 offices across India", with coverage "across the northern, central, and parts of eastern and southern regions of India".
- Certification-led credentials: "A Government of India Recognised Export House", ISO 9001:2015 & 14001:2015 certified, GOTS approved, ZDHC gateway registered, plus Bluesign and ZDHC certification cited for the dyestuff business.
- Customer sets are named per division: farmers via 800 distributors (fertilisers), cattle & poultry feed manufacturers (animal health & nutrition), manufacturers of synthetic dyes (dye intermediates), and textile dyeing, "particularly for cellulosic fibers (cotton, flax, and wool)" (dyestuff).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Land acquisition] "the Company acquired approximately 30,000 sq. metres of land at Lote Parshuram for Rs. 9.33 Cr, adjacent to its existing Unit 1", to support future expansion at the existing manufacturing location.
- [M&A history] 100% equity acquisition of Kisan Phosphates Pvt Ltd (2018-2019 diversification phase) and 100% equity acquisition of Madhya Bharat Phosphate Pvt Ltd (2021), the latter alongside commencing A.H.N.F production at MBPPL Unit 2 in Madhya Pradesh.
- [Operating environment] Management attributes Q1 FY27 volume declines in both segments to "ongoing global supply chain challenges and elevated raw material prices" and "the prevailing operating environment", with improved realisations offsetting lower volumes.
- [Prior infrastructure] At KPPL the company "Installed sulphuric acid and captive power plants utilizing a waste heat boiler and commissioned a 200 TPD granulation plant" (2016-17), and completed additional capacity of 32,000 MTPA in KPPL (2023).
- [Promoter-led board] Mr. Punit Makharia is Chairman & Managing Director and Mr. Gautam Makharia is Joint Managing Director, alongside three Non-Executive Independent Directors and one Non-Executive Non-Independent Director.
